verdict: Yes, but only with a clear sourcing or flavour edge, because makhana is now one of the most crowded healthy-snack categories. Demand is real and growing, Bihar's Mithila makhana has a GI tag, and the Union Budget 2025 announced a Makhana Board. The risk is price competition and swings in raw makhana prices, so margins depend on buying well.
angle: Most of India's makhana comes from Bihar's Mithila region, where it is harvested from ponds and popped by hand. A brand that buys graded makhana directly from processors in districts such as Darbhanga and Madhubani controls quality and cost in a way that brands buying from city wholesalers can't. Pair that with a flavour range for one audience (gym-goers, kids' tiffins or office snacking) and you have something distinct.

faq.q: How much does it cost to start a makhana snacks brand?
faq.a: With a co-packer roasting and flavouring for you, ₹2–5 lakh covers raw makhana, packaging, FSSAI licence and launch marketing for three flavours. Your own roasting line costs ₹25 lakh or more.
Buy graded makhana directly from processors in Bihar's Mithila region. It's usually cheaper than city wholesale, and you can choose the size grade, which affects taste and price.

faq.q: Is there government support for makhana businesses?
faq.a: Makhana processing qualifies for PMFME, which gives a 35% capital subsidy up to ₹10 lakh for micro food units. The Union Budget 2025 also announced a Makhana Board for Bihar.

faq.q: What margin do makhana brands make?
faq.a: Selling through distributors or quick commerce, expect to keep 8–15% of MRP after all costs. Selling multi-packs on your own website earns considerably more per order.
